newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. businessmen praise Mexico govt policies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. businessmen praise Mexico govt policies.

text.p: U.S. businessmen said Monday they were confident Mexico's economy was on track for recovery and praised President Ernesto Zedillo's handling of the country's guerrilla problems.

Members of a U.S.-Mexico bilateral business committee told reporters after meeting Zedillo that they believed the Mexican peso would gradually gain strength and that investments in the country would continue.
"In the long term the Mexican peso will look very good," committee president Robert Mosbacher said.

Mosbacher, who served as Commerce Secretary during the presidency of George Bush, declined comment on the possible risks of another Mexican peso devaluation. The peso lost more than two percent against the dollar last week.
He also praised as "realistic" the government's 1997 economic programme, agreed with business and unions Saturday.

Committee vice-president John Hennessy said foreign investment in Mexico had been more gradual than in the boom years of 1993 and 1994 but said this was "understandable and perhaps more stable because there was a lot of speculation in the flows of money and capital".
The current flow, he said, was "healthy and sustainable".
The honorary president of the American Association of the Council of the Americas, David Rockefeller, said the appearance of guerrilla movements in Mexico had been closely followed in the U.S.

"In fact this has caused concern in our country but people who have followed the situation closely feel that President Zedillo has handled this with great skill, patience and a good deal of firmness" he said.
